(1) 
The section heading is amended to read as follows:



“development of sources of energy on or for military installations”.



 
    (2) Subsection (b)(1) is amended by inserting “or on private property” after “jurisdiction”,

fable.w: This section only makes technical amendments: it rewrites a section heading and inserts a phrase extending the provision to private property. The mention of private property might suggest that outside parties are involved, but the text sets up no consultation, hearing, comment period, rulemaking, advisory body, or right to sue. No party outside the federal government is brought into any federal decision.
fable.s: Subsection (b)(1) is amended by inserting “or on private property” after “jurisdiction”

opus.w: This section is a technical amendment. It renames a section heading and adds private property to the places where military energy sources may be developed. No outside party is consulted or given a role in a federal decision. Mentioning private property only describes a location, so it does not count as participation by an outside party.
opus.s: Subsection (b)(1) is amended by inserting “or on private property” after “jurisdiction”
opus.b: 1. **Thinking it through.** The tempting reading is that "private property" brings in outside parties such as private landowners. That fails against the definition. The amendment only widens where energy development may take place. It sets up no consultation, comment period, hearing, advisory body, or right to sue for anyone outside the federal government. The rest is a heading change.

qwen_chat.w: This section is a legislative amendment that expands the geographic scope of a program to include private property. It does not contain any language requiring the federal government to consult, coordinate with, or seek input from private landowners or any other outside parties. The mere inclusion of private property in the scope of authority does not constitute a participation requirement.
qwen_chat.s: (2) Subsection (b)(1) is amended by inserting “or on private property” after “jurisdiction”,
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that amending the statute to include "private property" implies some form of consultation or coordination with private landowners. However, the text provided is merely a legislative amendment instruction changing the scope of authority; it does not explicitly mandate any process for consulting, coordinating with, or obtaining input from private parties. It simply expands the geographic scope where the Secretary can act. Without explicit language requiring interaction with outsiders, this is just a change in statutory scope, not a participation mechanism.
